A fresh vow to save my sister.
Now to put everything into that work—except permission for this simple arrangement was not available.

Not because of my job. My leave from the company had to be extended again.

The Head had announced the Hair-Binding Ceremony.

Under Minato clan law, the ritual office—the priestess-princess's position—passed to the next girl at a fixed age. Before that age, forbidden. After that age, also forbidden. The calendar had spoken.

A remarkable member of the family, the calendar. Never ill, never tired, never asked to kneel through half a day of ceremony. Just hang there and be correct. Meanwhile the living girl had to arrange her recovery around it. Thoda ruk jao? Wait a little? No, apparently the paper had very strict principles. I would have liked to see it carry Hikaru into the sanctuary.

Hikaru had fallen ill just before the succession rite. For the Head, surely the greatest frustration of his old age. The last major duty of his generation, almost settled—and then this interruption.

But Doctor Mengele's treatment had set Hikaru's body on the way to recovery. Since then, not one fit.

The successor's work in the Hair-Binding Ceremony was to perform the prescribed rites in the prescribed manner. Complicated, tedious, certainly. Skill and independent judgment, however, were not required. Even now, with somebody to assist her, Hikaru could manage it.

For the Head, presumably: this opportunity must not escape. The doctor had barely gone home before a date was fixed.

I would have preferred more rest first. Let Hikaru recover her strength. The ceremony took half a day; the physical burden was considerable. Precisely why it had been impossible until now.

Even now, the danger was far from gone. But after the great favour of bringing the doctor, neither my foster mother nor I could object very strongly to the Head's face.

Support her carefully, and perhaps we could lighten the burden...
With that thought, reluctantly, we compromised. The senior house would have its way.

And today—

妹を救うと、心も新たに誓い――
　しかし、ただその為に邁進する事は許されなかった。

　仕事があるから、ではない。
　会社への休暇願いは、延長を余儀なくされた。

　本家が、髪上げの儀の実施を宣言したからだ。

　皆斗家法において、湊斗の<ruby>祀司<rt>しし</rt></ruby>――即ち<ruby>巫姫<rt>かんなぎ</rt></ruby>の継承
は、次代たるべき女子が一定の年齢に達するをもって
行うものとされている。
　その年齢より前でも、後でもならない。

　継承儀礼――髪上げの儀を目前にして光が病に倒れ
たことは、本家が老境に入って迎えた最大の痛恨事で
あったに違いない。当代の、最後の大事が片付こうと
したところで、横槍を差されてしまったのだから。

　だが、メンゲレ博士の治療によって光の肉体は快方
に向かった。
　あれ以来、発作は一度も起こしていない。

　髪上げの儀の際、継承者がすべきは定められた儀礼
を定められた通りにこなすだけだ。それは複雑にして
煩雑だが、別に技術も自己判断も必要ない。
　今の光でも、介添人が付けばできる事だった。

　本家にしてみれば、この機を逃してなるものか――
というところであったのだろう。
　博士が帰国するや否やのうちに、もう儀式の日取り
まで決めてしまっていた。

　俺としては、今しばらくは光を休ませ、体力を取り
戻させてからにしたかった。
　髪上げの儀は半日にも渡り、体力負担は少なくない。
だからこれまでは無理だったのだ。

　今とても、まだまだ危うい。
　だが、博士の招聘で大恩を<ruby>蒙<rt>こうむ</rt></ruby>った以上、俺も養母も
本家に面と向かって強い事は言えなかった。

　心を配って補佐すれば、光の負担も軽くしてやれる
だろう……。
　そう考え、やむなく妥協して、本家の要望に従った。


　そして、今日――――

Whenever my foster mother recited the ritual prayer, it was magnificent. Such an even tone, and inside it, depth beyond explanation.

Years of repetition. Thousands of times, tens of thousands. Only then could a chant reach this state. The attendees were required to keep their heads lowered, but even without the rule, the head would have lowered itself.

From my seat at the very end, I sent a look sliding along the floor. Discourteous? Yes. Unavoidable? Also yes. I had no right to attend in the first place. Now that I had been allowed in, neglecting my assigned duty would be a fine achievement.

Beyond the Head and the important people of the Minato houses, seated in two rows, Hikaru waited beside her mother.

Leaning against the back of her floor chair, vacant, apparently listening. ...For now, nothing wrong. The preliminary rites before this main ceremony must already have tired her, but she did not seem past her limit yet.

That chair was not in accordance with ritual etiquette. Not even remotely. The Head had expressed considerable displeasure, but necessary was necessary. Had we been allowed to lay her flat, different matter.

At this rate, we should finish safely.
No carelessness on the strength of that thought, though.

The Head's nerves had received enough attention from us. If anything happened, we must act immediately. I looked away, but my awareness stayed fixed on Hikaru.

養母の祝詞奏上はいつ聴いても見事なものだった。
　平板な調子の中に得も言われぬ深みがある。

　何年にも渡り、何千回何万回と繰り返して、初めて
完成する詠唱だ。
　奏上中、参列者は面を伏せて待つのが決まりだが、
そんなものが無くとも自然と頭は下がったろう。

　末席から、床の上を滑らせるようにして視線を投げ、
様子を窺う。
　非礼だが仕方ない。本来参列の資格を持たないにも
拘わらず列席している以上、役目に手は抜けなかった。

　本家をはじめ、皆斗諸家の要人らが左右二列に分か
れて居並ぶ向こう。
　母に付き従う格好で、光がいる。

　座椅子に背をもたれさせ、茫としながら祝詞に耳を
預けているようだった。……今のところ、異変はない。
　この祭殿での本儀礼に先立つ諸儀で既に疲労が蓄積
している筈だが、まだ限度を超える程ではないようだ。

　あの座椅子は礼法に沿うものである筈もなく、本家
の不興を買うこと<ruby>夥<rt>おびただ</rt></ruby>しかったが、やはり必要な措置で
はあった。
　寝転がしておいても良いならまた話は変わるが。

　この分ならば、最後まで無事に済むだろう。
　しかし油断はできない。

　本家の神経をこれ以上逆撫でしない為にも、もし何
かあった際には迅速に対処できるよう備えておかねば
ならなかった。
　俺は視線を外しつつも、光の様子に意識を集めた。

My foster mother finished the prayer without interruption. At an ordinary observance, only the sacred food and tamagushi branches remained to be offered.

Today, different arrangements. Next came the Presentation, as it was commonly called: the heart of the Hair-Binding Ceremony.

The Minato dignitaries withdrew.◆
...In due course, they returned.

Warrior dress.
Swords in hand.

Armed, they were. Ceremonial equipment only, admittedly.

Now the ceremony returned to its beginning. Once more, open the sacred doors before the deity.

Yes, those doors were already open. They had been opened before the prayer. Offer a prayer to the enshrined deity while keeping the doors shut, and what would be the point?

But behind those doors—the ones opened for ordinary worship—stood another pair. The Inner Sacred Doors.

Only at especially important rites, such as this one, were they opened. What lay sealed inside did not meet the outside air even once a year.

Thick iron. More castle gate than door. Several sets of nearly antique battle gear gave little metallic rattles. Perhaps the sight had made their occupants nervous.

These people at the heart of the Minato clan knew.
Why they carried weapons. Why the inner doors were iron.

Following the prescribed form, my foster mother unlocked them with the sacred key. A heavy, solid sound announced that something had been released.

She put the key back, advanced on her knees, took her appointed position and laid hands on the doors. They began to open.

All of us, myself included, bent forward together and sounded the ceremonial warning cry. Ooooooh.

Twice. Once for the left door, once for the right.
The Inner Sacred Doors were open.

Beyond them stood the Minato family's deepest secret.

養母の祝詞が滞りなく終わる。
　常の祭事であれば、この後は神饌や玉串を奉るだけ
だ。

　だが今日は違う。
　この次には『顔見せ』と通称される、髪上げの儀の
肝と言うべき祭礼が入る。

　皆斗の歴々が一度退場。◆
　……やがて戻る。

　武家装束に身を固め。
　太刀を携え。

　彼らは武装・・していた。
　あくまで儀礼用のものに過ぎないが。

　そして儀式は一度、始まりへと戻る。
　再び、御扉――神前の扉を開くのだ。

　無論、それは既に開かれている。
　祝詞の奏上の前に。祝詞は祭神に捧げるのだから、
その前に扉を開かねば意味がない。

　だがその際に――つまりは通常の祭儀において開か
れる御扉の奥には、もう一枚の、別の御扉があるのだ。
　奥御扉と云う。

　これはこの髪上げの儀など、特に重要な祭事でしか
開かれない。
　扉の中に封じられたものは年に一度も外気と交わら
ないのだ。

　分厚い鉄扉はさながら城門である。
　骨董品も同然の戦支度が幾つか、それを見てか緊張
に震えて細かな金属音を鳴らし立てた。

　皆斗一族の枢要たる彼らは皆、知っている。
　自らの武装の意味も。鉄の奥御扉の意味も。

　作法通り、養母が御鑰みかぎを用いて門の錠を外す。
　重く固い音が、何か・・の開放を告げた。

　養母は鑰を戻し、今度は扉を開けるために膝進しっしん。
　所定の座に着き、手を掛ける。扉を開き始める。

　それに合わせて、列席者（俺を含む）は一斉に前傾。
　おおおおぅ――と警蹕けいひつを合唱する。

　左右の扉を開けるため、それを二回。
　奥御扉の開扉が完了する。

　そうして――その向こう。
　皆斗家の最秘は、顕れていた。

One, a silver queen ant.
One, a crimson spider.

Insect shapes. Insect sizes, absolutely not. Each had a body to match a human being's.

Steel.
Steel forged at the very limit of craftsmanship.

Tsurugi.
Not the mass-produced suits that dominated modern battlefields, either.

A smith gave everything—body and soul—or they could not be completed.
True-forged tsurugi.

From ancient times to the present, only the warrior class had the right to own tsurugi. Yet through every change in its own standing, the Minato clan had kept these two. Unused, passed from generation to generation. ...In the strictest secrecy.

An imperial command to seal away an evil thing had brought the clan to this land. These tsurugi were that thing. The duty handed to every generation, standing here before us.

Their names, their origins—I knew little in detail. Only that they must never be released. But one look made the matter plain. Something monstrously unnatural hung about them. Calamity had a presence here.

One look did what a thousand explanations could not. Anybody seeing them would reach the same conclusion: keep them sealed. Forever would not be too long.

Do not touch.
Do not speak of them.

The greatest taboo of the Minato clan.

Not a bloodstain, not a speck of dust on that shining armour. Such beauty, and such horror in it...

A small glance from my foster mother brought me back. Enough admiration of the shiny metal. She was supporting Hikaru, somehow getting her upright, preparing to guide her before the tsurugi.

A few steps only. For Hikaru now, a very harsh journey. If trouble was coming, this was its best opportunity. And I was standing there gawking. Excellent work.

I collected myself and watched Hikaru's back. Perhaps the practice we had given her limbs for this day had helped. Half carried by my foster mother, she could take one unsteady step, then another.

Walking and such motions learned by the body—apparently, with another person's prompting, she could just about perform them. The priestess-princess carrying her successor piggyback would not have presented much dignity. A considerable mercy, this.

Somehow, wobbling, Hikaru reached the divine seat. The breath of relief filling the sanctuary probably came from everyone except her.

The day's most important business, the Presentation, was almost complete. The two tsurugi receiving the rites were now considered duly informed: the priestess-princess conducting Minato worship was to change.

Naturally, everyone relaxed a little.

—Perhaps that was where we went wrong.

en.html:
At the sudden noise, everybody jumped. Internally. In the face. Actual jumping would have required a shortage of self-control not represented in this gathering.

Instead, every gaze landed at one point: the feet of a horrified elderly attendee.

A piece of metal lay there. An ornament from his sword. Somehow, he had dropped it.

The Head gave him a look full of concentrated fury. In a panic the man snatched the ornament up and tucked it inside his clothes.

—That was all.
That incident, at least.

But something else had happened at the same time.
I had seen it. How it happened, I could not say.

Had Hikaru moved at the noise? Or had my foster mother, supporting her, turned in surprise and brought it about?

The cause, unknown.
The result, very much present.

Hikaru's fingertips were caught on the silver ant.
The tsurugi we had been strictly forbidden to touch—even during the ceremony.

Three people. Three messages exchanged by eye.

The Head's fury had the destructive power of a death ray. Strongest message, without question.
My foster mother's, however, had the most practical value.

'Nothing was seen. Agreed?'

..................

What else was there to do? The Head let out a breath through grinding teeth. Mine came with a bitter smile.

Had the tsurugi grown enormous and started breathing fire the moment she touched it, different matter. It had done no such thing. Anger would serve what purpose? First, finish the ceremony safely.

...Presumably the Head had to keep explaining this to himself until he accepted it. For an old clan leader who placed obedience to the rules above everything, what an ordeal. I felt for him. He would not thank me for that either.

At least let the rest proceed peacefully. We owed him that much. I turned my attention back to Hikaru.

—That very instant.
The final disturbance.

Human law binds him too, body and mind. By force I could seize his body. His heart, however, would not follow orders.

He would not willingly return to Hikaru.
Then what was the use?

...Therefore.
THAT LAW MUST GO!

Hikaru becomes a god—
and gets her father back LEGALLY!

Perfect. Full legality.
Then Father will acknowledge Hikaru!

Then he will let his daughter return to his arms!

HAAN!!

A prison. Yes. This is a prison.
All this time, a prison.

And I thought it had no key...

These iron shackles are Mother's hands, refusing my wish for Father.
These iron shackles are everybody's hands, refusing that wish.

YOUR EXISTENCE IS NOT PERMITTED.
So stay there. The world has spoken.

I thought resistance was impossible. No—even the idea of resisting had never entered my head.

...But that was wrong.
With martial power, this oppression can be overturned.

Stronger than these bastards, and the prison breaks to powder. Is that not so!?

The world bows to me. The world welcomes me as A GOD!

And Hikaru—
Hikaru can TAKE FATHER BACK!!
